column11: Welireg, CMS Medicare Part D 2024 (drug_demand, brand Welireg): $205,460,495.55 over 1,896 beneficiaries = $108,365.24 a beneficiary a year. This is the basis the book prices on and the same method amgn_abp_206.csv uses. For scale rather than for the arithmetic, the unit price under it is $205,460,495.55 over 634,437 dosage units = $323.847 a tablet, and the label dose of 120 mg once daily is three 40 mg tablets a day, so a full labelled year of 1,095 tablets is $354,612 gross
column12: a price per patient treated in a year, not per full year on drug, which is what makes it consistent with discontinuation_pct below: $108,365 / $354,612 = 0.3056, exactly the share of a labelled year the stopping rate is derived from. Pairing the $354,612 labelled year with the same 0.6944 would count the shortfall twice. The per-beneficiary figure fell from 2023 to 2024, $132,061 to $108,365, which is not a price cut: 2024 is the year the advanced renal cell carcinoma claim brought 1,443 new beneficiaries in, and a cohort full of mid-year starters fills less of a year. No Merck WAC disclosure for Welireg was reachable, and CMS NADAC carries no belzutifan row because it is a limited-distribution specialty product, so the CMS unit price above is the only openable per-tablet figure

column11: the house Part D gross-to-net, measured rather than assumed: CMS Part D spending is gross of manufacturer rebates, and halving a gross CMS figure lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net annual prices across the nine cycle-one Inflation Reduction Act drugs that carry a demand row, spread 65% to 167% (backend/gross_to_net.py). Belzutifan is an oral tablet dispensed under Part D, which is the basis that module was calibrated on
column12: the weakest row in this file and probably too deep. Net at 0.5 is $54,183 a patient treated in a year. Direction: the module was calibrated on the cycle-one negotiated drugs, which are Eliquis, Jardiance, Xarelto, Januvia, Farxiga, Entresto, Enbrel, Imbruvica, Stelara and NovoLog, mostly crowded retail classes with deep formulary rebates. Belzutifan is the only HIF-2-alpha inhibitor on the market, orphan in von Hippel-Lindau disease and without a direct substitute in post-TKI clear cell renal cell carcinoma, and a drug with no therapeutic alternative does not pay for formulary position. The book's own oral oncology figure, 0.18, is the other end of the range and would put net at $88,859. The house Part D basis is carried rather than the oral oncology one because this row's anchor is a CMS gross Part D figure, which is what that basis was measured against, and because taking the shallow end would be adjusting a number upward on a hunch. Replace it the day a belzutifan-specific net is disclosed

column11: measured on Welireg's own patients: drug_demand Welireg, CMS Medicare Part D 2024, 634,437 dosage units over 1,896 beneficiaries = 334.62 tablets a beneficiary. the current WELIREG label, DailyMed SPL setid 13e15ee0-d679-4fa9-9430-e2e2170474da, version 13, effective 2026-10-12 gives 120 mg once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, which is three 40 mg tablets a day and 1,095 tablets a labelled year. 334.62 / 1,095 = 0.3056 of a labelled year, and 1 - 0.3056 = 0.6944 of the stock stops each year
column12: measured on the same beneficiaries the price above is quoted on, which is the point of the basis. The implied hazard is 1.185 a year, a median 7.0 months on drug, which sits where a published duration would: LITESPARK-005 (NCT04195750), the trial the advanced renal cell carcinoma claim rests on, reported median progression-free survival of 5.6 months on belzutifan. Against it: 2024 is the launch year of that claim and brought 1,443 new beneficiaries into a base of 453, so the cohort is unusually full of part-year starters and this is the high end of the range. The two quieter years before it, when the base was almost all von Hippel-Lindau patients who stay on for years, still read 0.6008 and 0.6293, so the measurement is not only a launch artefact

column11: two published shares multiplied. 47.9% of patients starting first-line therapy for HR-positive HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer went on to a second line (Goyal et al., Breast Cancer Res Treat 2023, doi:10.1007/s10549-022-06845-4: 1,581 of 3,244, SEER-Medicare 2010-2019), the same share the PF-07248144 row in this book already takes on this pool. Of those second lines, 17.7% are endocrine monotherapy (Mahtani et al., Breast 2026, doi:10.1016/j.breast.2026.104732), which is precisely the control arm of LITESPARK-029: fulvestrant or exemestane alone, after progression on endocrine therapy with a CDK4/6 inhibitor. 0.479 x 0.177 = 0.0848, about 13,600 of the prevalent pool and 5,500 a year
column12: the tighter of two readings and knowably low, which is said rather than quietly fixed. The wider reading is every second line that is not chemotherapy, 0.479 x (1 - 0.316) = 0.328, since the trial's only treatment exclusions are prior fulvestrant, prior chemotherapy and prior PARP inhibition in the non-curative setting (NCT06428396 eligibility). The narrow share is carried because belzutifan with fulvestrant competes for the patient a physician would otherwise put on single-agent endocrine therapy, not for the patient going to a CDK4/6 rechallenge or to an antibody-drug conjugate. Taking the wider share would raise the layer roughly fourfold

column11: a share of the pool above, set against what the molecule has to displace
column12: a judgement, and a cautious one. What it displaces is thin on paper, single-agent fulvestrant or exemestane, which is the trial's own control arm and the reason the trial is designed this way. What makes it hard is everything else now sitting in that line: capivasertib for PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN altered tumours, elacestrant for ESR1 mutants, everolimus with exemestane, and the antibody-drug conjugates pulling the fitter patients out of endocrine therapy earlier. Belzutifan has no published breast cancer efficacy at all, which is what LITESPARK-029 is for, and a hypoxia-inducible factor inhibitor has no established biomarker in this disease to select on. A tenth of the eligible pool is a tenth of a pool that is already the narrow reading

column11: a different disease from any the label names, so none of this pool sits in the 716mm USD. the current WELIREG label, DailyMed SPL setid 13e15ee0-d679-4fa9-9430-e2e2170474da, version 13, effective 2026-10-12 carries exactly three indications: von Hippel-Lindau disease associated renal cell carcinoma, central nervous system haemangioblastoma or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour; renal cell carcinoma with a clear cell component, adjuvant with pembrolizumab and advanced with lenvatinib or as monotherapy after a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor and a VEGF-TKI; and pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma. Breast cancer appears nowhere on it
